# markdown-s2 — Safe Markdown → HTML renderer (tier S2) ## Module: `src/markdown.js` (ES module) - `export function render(markdown: string, { headingIds = false } = {}): string` → HTML. - `export function toc(markdown: string): Array<{ level: number, text: string, slug: string }>` — every ATX/setext heading in document order; `text` is the heading's plain text (inline markup removed). - `export function slugify(text: string, seen?: Map)` — GitHub-style slug: lower-case; remove every character that is not a letter, digit, space, `-` or `_`; spaces → `-`. When a `Map` of previously seen slugs is passed, repeated slugs get `-1`, `-2`, … suffixes. `toc` and `headingIds` use one map per document. ## Output conventions Follow CommonMark 0.31 HTML output (as produced by the reference implementation commonmark.js) plus GFM tables and strikethrough, except where this spec says otherwise. Insignificant whitespace between block-level tags is not significant to the tests; `
`/`
`, `
`/`
`, ``/`` are equivalent; table alignment may be expressed as `align="left"` or `style="text-align:left"`. Required features: - ATX headings `#`…`######` (closing `#`s stripped), setext headings (`===`, `---`). With `headingIds: true`, headings get `id=""`: `

My title

`. - Paragraphs; soft line breaks preserved as `\n`; hard breaks via two trailing spaces or a trailing backslash → `
`. - Emphasis/strong with `*` and `_` (CommonMark rules incl. no intraword `_` emphasis), `***x***` → `x`; GFM `~~strike~~` → ``. - Code spans (multi-backtick delimiters, one leading/trailing space stripped when both present). - Fenced code blocks (``` and ~~~, info string → `class="language-"`) and indented code blocks. - Blockquotes (nested, with lazy continuation lines), thematic breaks (`---`, `***`, `___`). - Bullet lists (`-`, `*`, `+`) and ordered lists (`1.` / `1)`, `start` attribute when not 1), nesting by indentation, tight vs loose lists (`

  • ` when loose). - Inline links `[t](url "title")`, images `![alt](src "title")`, reference links `[t][ref]`, `[ref]` with definitions `[ref]: url "title"` (case-insensitive labels), autolinks `` and `<>` (→ `mailto:`). - Backslash escapes; HTML-escape `& < > "` in text, attributes and code. - GFM pipe tables with header row, delimiter row, optional alignment (`:--`, `:-:`, `--:`), inline markup in cells, `\|` escapes. ## Safety (deliberate deviation from CommonMark) - Raw HTML (block and inline) is NOT passed through: it is rendered as escaped text, e.g. `` → `

    <script>x</script>

    `. - Link/image URLs with schemes `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:` or `data:` (except `data:image/png|gif|jpeg|webp;`) are replaced by `#`. ## CLI: `src/cli.js` `node src/cli.js [--toc] [--ids]` prints HTML (or with `--toc`, the TOC as JSON) to stdout. Reads stdin when the file argument is `-`. package.json tests: public tests/public: smoke.test.js { "name": "markdown-s2", "version": "1.0.0", "type": "module", "scripts": { "test": "node --test" } } import { test } from 'node:test'; import assert from 'node:assert/strict'; import { render } from '../../src/markdown.js'; const n = s => s.replace(/\s*(<\/?(?:p|h[1-6]|ul|ol|li|blockquote|pre|table|thead|tbody|tr|th|td|hr)\b[^>]*>)\s*/g, '$1').trim(); test('heading + paragraph', () => { assert.equal(n(render('# Hi\n\nSome *text*.')), '

    Hi

    Some text.

    '); }); test('raw html escaped', () => { assert.equal(n(render('x')), '

    <b>x</b>

    '); });

content.text:
I built the safe Markdown renderer from SPEC.md on top of a vendored copy of **markdown-it 14.1.0** (MIT), rather than writing a parser from scratch. `node --test` passes: 4 of 4, which covers the 2 public smoke tests and 2 of my own. **How I followed the reuse protocol:** I searched GitHub (finding micromark, remarkable and cmark-gfm), Stack Overflow (nothing useful) and npm. I picked markdown-it because it already does CommonMark plus GFM tables and strikethrough, and its built-in setting for raw HTML already escapes it as text. I fetched it and its five dependencies from npm (entities under BSD-2-Clause, mdurl, uc.micro, linkify-it and punycode.js under MIT) and copied them into `src/vendor/`. The only change to that code is rewriting the package imports as relative paths, so it runs with no npm dependencies. **What I wrote myself:** - **`src/markdown.js`** is a thin layer over markdown-it: - `render(md, { headingIds })` escapes raw HTML, uses `
` and ``, and outputs strikethrough as ``. - Links and images using `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:` or `data:` get `#` as their URL. The allowed image `data:` types are kept. - Heading ids come from the heading's plain text, with one slug map per document. - `toc(md)` lists every ATX and setext heading as `{level, text, slug}`, with inline markup removed from `text`. - `slugify(text, seen?)` makes GitHub-style slugs and adds `-1`, `-2`, … for repeats when a `Map` is passed. - **`src/cli.js`** supports `node src/cli.js [--toc] [--ids]`, reading stdin when the file is `-`. - **`tests/public/extra.test.js`** checks strikethrough, heading ids, unsafe URLs, `toc` and slugify. **Where the hidden tests might catch differences:** - markdown-it's output is very close to commonmark.js but may not match it exactly in every edge case, and I didn't check it against the CommonMark spec examples. - Table alignment is written as `style="text-align:..."`, which SPEC.md accepts. - Only `~~double~~` tildes make strikethrough; a single `~x~` stays plain text. - `slugify` keeps only letters, digits, spaces, `-` and `_`, as the spec says. Accent marks typed as separate characters are therefore removed, which may not match GitHub's own slugs. Licenses and sources are recorded in `PROVENANCE.json` and `src/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, and each vendored package keeps its own LICENSE file.
